chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said:
I said to him: A man forgot to pronounce the opening takbīrah until he said the takbīrah for rukūʿ. He said: It suffices him.

The proper understanding of this report as well is what we stated regarding the previous reports: that it is not established that he did not pronounce the opening takbīrah. So if he pronounces the takbīrah for rukūʿ, that suffices for the takbīrah about which we said he should take precaution with it. But if omitting it were established with certainty, then it would be necessary to restart the salat (prayer), as we have explained.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him and was deemed adequate
key_terms.اسْتِئْنَافِ الصَّلَاةِ: restarting the salat (prayer) from the beginning
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةَ الِافْتِتَاحِ: the opening takbīrah that begins the salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَسْتَظْهِرَ: to act with precaution or added care

ai.seo_question: Does the takbīrah for rukūʿ suffice if someone forgot Takbīrat al-Iftitāḥ in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of one who forgets Takbīrat al-Iftitāḥ until reaching the takbīrah of rukūʿ. The explanation given is that the case is understood as one in which omission of the opening takbīrah is not certain; otherwise, if its omission were certain, the salat (prayer) would need to be restarted.
